records.source: וַיִּקְרָ֣א מֹשֶׁה֮ אֶל־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם שְׁמַ֤ע יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶת־הַחֻקִּ֣ים וְאֶת־הַמִּשְׁפָּטִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֧ר אָנֹכִ֛י דֹּבֵ֥ר בְּאָזְנֵיכֶ֖ם הַיּ֑וֹם וּלְמַדְתֶּ֣ם אֹתָ֔ם וּשְׁמַרְתֶּ֖ם לַעֲשֹׂתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And called Moses to all Israel and said to them, hear, Israel, the statutes and the judgments which I [am] speaking in your ears the day, and you shall learn them and you shall keep to do them.
pieces: Moses summoned all Israel and said to them, "Hear, Israel, the statutes and rulings that I am announcing to you today. Learn them and be careful to do them.

L.1: And Moses called to all Israel and said to them, "Hear, Israel, the statutes and the judgments that I [am] speaking in your ears today, and you shall learn them and take care to do them.

R.1: Moses called all the people of Israel together and said to them, "Listen, Israel! Today I am telling you the laws and rules. Learn them and make sure you obey them.

decisions.choice: and said to them: the start of Moses' second speech
decisions.reason: A short narrative line introduces Moses' words, which begin with "Hear, Israel" and run without a break to 26:19. The first speech ended at 4:40, and 4:44-49 described the setting. This second speech holds the ten words (verses 6-21) and the laws of chapters 12-26.

decisions.choice: statutes and judgments: the laws and the rulings Moses is about to teach
decisions.reason: The pair names the whole body of law as fixed rules (statutes) and decisions for cases (judgments), as in 4:1, 5 and 4:45. Verse 31 adds "the commandment" and says Moses received all of it from God at Horeb.

decisions.choice: speaking in your ears: speaking to you directly, so that you hear it
decisions.reason: To speak "in someone's ears" is to say it aloud in their hearing (31:28, 30; Genesis 23:13). Moses stresses that the people hear it from him in person today.

decisions.choice: learn them and keep them, to do them: hearing leads to learning, and learning to doing
decisions.reason: The three verbs form a chain that runs through Deuteronomy: hear, learn, keep, do (4:1, 10; 6:1-3; 31:12). "Keep" means to watch over, take care, and with "to do" it means to be careful to carry the laws out.

decisions.choice: Listen, Israel!
decisions.reason: Readable uses the everyday word "listen" here. The same call opens 6:4, where every level keeps "Hear, Israel".

records.heading: The Ten Words

records.source: יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ כָּרַ֥ת עִמָּ֛נוּ בְּרִ֖ית בְּחֹרֵֽב׃
records.gloss: Yahweh our God cut with us a covenant at Horeb.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} our God made a covenant with us at Horeb.

L.2: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} our God made a covenant with us at Horeb.

R.2: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} our God made a covenant with us at Mount Horeb.

decisions.choice: Horeb: the mountain called Sinai in Exodus
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy calls the mountain of the covenant Horeb (1:6; 4:10, 15). Exodus uses both names for it (Exodus 3:1; 19:11, 20). The covenant was made there about forty years before this speech (1:3).

decisions.choice: cut a covenant: make a binding agreement
decisions.reason: The verb is "cut". The phrase may come from the custom of cutting animals in two when a covenant was sworn (Genesis 15:9-18; Jeremiah 34:18). It had become the ordinary way to say "make a covenant".

decisions.choice: Mount Horeb
decisions.reason: Readable adds "Mount" so that new readers know Horeb is the mountain of verse 4.

records.source: לֹ֣א אֶת־אֲבֹתֵ֔ינוּ כָּרַ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־הַבְּרִ֣ית הַזֹּ֑את כִּ֣י אִתָּ֗נוּ אֲנַ֨חְנוּ אֵ֥לֶּה פֹ֛ה הַיּ֖וֹם כֻּלָּ֥נוּ חַיִּֽים׃
records.gloss: Not with our fathers cut Yahweh the covenant the this, but with us, we, these here the day, all of us living.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} did not make this covenant with our fathers; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made it with us, the ones here today, all of us still alive.

L.3: Not with our fathers did {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} make this covenant, but with us, we, these [who are] here today, all of us living.

R.3: This covenant was not made with our ancestors. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} made it with us, every one of us here today who is still living.

decisions.choice: not with our fathers, but with us: the covenant binds this generation directly
alternatives: not only with our fathers, but also with us
not with the patriarchs, but with us
decisions.reason: Most of the adults who stood at Horeb had died in the wilderness (2:14-16), and many who now listen were children then. Moses insists that the covenant was made with them, not as something handed down from the past. The "fathers" may be that dead generation, and then the saying means "not only with them, but with us", a way of speaking that puts all the weight on the second part. Or the fathers may be the patriarchs (4:31, 37; 7:8, 12), with whom God swore a covenant but to whom he did not give this one, and then the saying is meant just as it stands.

decisions.choice: with us, we, these here today, all of us living: heaped-up emphasis
decisions.reason: The Hebrew piles up words for the people present: "us", "we", "these", "here", "today", "all of us", "living". Each one presses the point that the covenant is theirs.

decisions.choice: with us, we, these [who are] here
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the repeated pronoun so the reader can see the emphasis (m2); Balanced and Readable carry it with "the ones here today, all of us" and "every one of us".

records.source: פָּנִ֣ים׀בְּפָנִ֗ים דִּבֶּ֨ר יְהוָ֧ה עִמָּכֶ֛ם בָּהָ֖ר מִתּ֥וֹךְ הָאֵֽשׁ׃
records.gloss: Face to face spoke Yahweh with you on the mountain from [the] midst of the fire,
pieces: On the mountain {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke with you face to face, out of the fire.

L.4: Face to face {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke with you on the mountain from the midst of the fire,

R.4: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to you directly on the mountain, from the middle of the fire.

decisions.choice: face to face: directly, in person, not through a messenger
decisions.reason: The phrase means that God himself spoke and the people heard his voice (verses 22-24; 4:12, 33, 36). It does not mean they saw him: they saw no form, only fire (4:12, 15). Exodus 33:11 and Numbers 12:8 use similar words of Moses alone; here the whole people heard the ten words for themselves.

decisions.choice: from the midst of the fire: the fire on the mountain at Horeb
decisions.reason: The mountain burned with fire when God came down on it (4:11; Exodus 19:18). Deuteronomy repeats that God spoke "from the midst of the fire" (4:12, 15, 33, 36; verses 22-26).

decisions.choice: directly
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom (m1) rather than keep "face to face", which could suggest that the people saw God.

records.source: אָ֠נֹכִי עֹמֵ֨ד בֵּין־יְהוָ֤ה וּבֵֽינֵיכֶם֙ בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔וא לְהַגִּ֥יד לָכֶ֖ם אֶת־דְּבַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה כִּ֤י יְרֵאתֶם֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י הָאֵ֔שׁ וְלֹֽא־עֲלִיתֶ֥ם בָּהָ֖ר לֵאמֹֽר׃ס
records.gloss: I [was] standing between Yahweh and between you at the time the that to declare to you [the] word of Yahweh, for you were afraid from [the] face of the fire and not you went up on the mountain, saying,
pieces: I was standing between {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and you at that time, to make known to you the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, since you were afraid of the fire and would not go up the mountain. He said:

L.5: I [was] standing between {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and you at that time to declare to you the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for you were afraid because of the fire and did not go up on the mountain, saying,

R.5: Back then I stood between {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and you. I was there to tell you what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said, because you were afraid of the fire and would not climb the mountain. This is what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said:

decisions.choice: saying: introduces the words God spoke, picking up verse 4
decisions.reason: Verse 5 is an aside about Moses' part in the events. The word "saying" at its end does not introduce words of Moses; it goes back to "Yahweh spoke with you" in verse 4 and opens God's own words in verses 6-21.

decisions.choice: standing between: Moses as the go-between for God and the people
decisions.reason: The people heard God's voice (verse 4), yet Moses stood between them because they feared the fire (verses 23-27; Exodus 20:18-21). The two statements fit together: they heard the ten words themselves, and Moses carried everything else God said to them (verse 31).

decisions.choice: afraid from the face of the fire: afraid because of the fire
decisions.reason: "From the face of" is a common way of saying "because of" or "in the presence of".

decisions.choice: He said: / This is what he said:
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable end the aside and begin a new sentence, so they supply who speaks, God (m1). Literal keeps the single word "saying".

records.source: אָֽנֹכִי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֧ר הוֹצֵאתִ֛יךָ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם מִבֵּ֥יתעֲבָדִֽים
records.gloss: I [am] Yahweh your God, who brought you out from [the] land of Egypt, from a house of slaves.
pieces: 'I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. I brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house where you were slaves.

L.6: 'I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, who brought you out from the land of Egypt, from the house of slaves.

R.6: 'I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. I brought you out of Egypt, where you lived as slaves.

decisions.choice: the ten words, as given in Exodus 20:2-17
decisions.reason: Moses repeats the ten words God spoke at Horeb (Exodus 20:2-17). Most of the wording is the same, but there are differences: the Sabbath is to be "kept" rather than "remembered" and is given a different reason (verses 12-15), two promises are added (verse 16), the last commands are joined by "and" (verses 18-21), and the coveting command names the wife first and adds the field (verse 21). Here the words are quoted within Moses' speech.

decisions.choice: I am Yahweh your God: God names himself before he commands
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 20:2, the words can also be read "I, Yahweh, am your God". Either way God first says who he is and what he has done, and the commands rest on that rescue.

decisions.choice: house of slaves: Egypt as the place of slavery
decisions.reason: The phrase pictures Egypt as a household where Israel served as slaves (6:12; 7:8; 8:14; Exodus 13:3; 20:2). Verse 15 returns to it.

decisions.choice: the ten words are counted in more than one way
decisions.reason: Scripture says there are ten (4:13; 10:4) but does not number them. Communities count them differently, as noted at Exodus 20:2; Deuteronomy's form of the last command (verse 21) is the basis of one of those counts.

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: "Slaves" at every level, since this is Israel's slavery in Egypt, as at Exodus 20:2.

records.source: לֹא־יִהְיֶ֥ה לְךָ֛אֱלֹהִ֥יםאֲחֵרִ֖יםעַל־פָּנָֽיַ
records.gloss: Not will be to you other gods on my face.
pieces: You shall have no other gods besides {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.7: There shall not be for you other gods before {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face.

R.7: Do not have any other gods except {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: on my face: besides me, in my presence
decisions.reason: The same words as Exodus 20:3. The phrase may mean "besides me", "in my presence" or "in defiance of me"; each reading forbids Israel any god but Yahweh.

decisions.choice: other gods: no rival may share Israel's loyalty
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy returns to this command again and again (6:14; 7:4; 8:19; 13:3).

decisions.choice: You shall not ... (Literal, Balanced); Do not ... (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 20, the commands use the form of a lasting prohibition. Literal and Balanced say "You shall not"; Readable uses the plain "Do not".

records.source: לֹֽ֣א־תַעֲשֶׂ֥ה לְךָ֥פֶ֨סֶל֙כָּל־תְּמוּנָ֔האֲשֶׁ֤רבַּשָּׁמַ֨יִם֙מִמַּ֔עַלוַאֲשֶׁ֥רבָּאָ֖רֶץמִתָּ֑חַתוַאֲשֶׁ֥ר בַּמַּ֖יִםמִתַּ֥חַתלָאָֽרֶץ
records.gloss: Not you shall make for yourself a carved image, any form which [is] in the heavens above and which [is] on the earth beneath and which [is] in the waters under the earth.
pieces: You shall not make yourself a carved idol in the form of anything in the heavens overhead, on the earth below, or in the waters beneath the earth.

L.8: You shall not make for yourself a carved image, any form that [is] in the heavens above, or that [is] on the earth beneath, or that [is] in the waters under the earth.

R.8: Do not make any idol for yourself in the shape of anything in the sky, on the land, or in the water below the land.

decisions.choice: a carved image, any form: an idol in the shape of anything
decisions.reason: Exodus 20:4 reads "a carved image and any form", two things forbidden. Here there is no "and", so "any form" describes the image: an idol shaped like anything in the world. The command forbids the same thing either way.

decisions.choice: no image of anything, including of Yahweh himself
decisions.reason: 4:15-18 gives the reason: Israel saw no form when Yahweh spoke from the fire, so they must make no image of anything, whether of another god or meant to stand for him.

decisions.choice: heavens, earth, waters under the earth: the whole created world
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 20:4, the three parts name everything there is: the birds and lights of the sky, land animals and people, and fish (4:16-19).

records.source: לֹא־תִשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֥הלָהֶ֖םוְלֹ֣א תָעָבְדֵ֑םכִּ֣י אָנֹכִ֞י יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ אֵ֣ל קַנָּ֔א פֹּ֠קֵד עֲוֺ֨ן אָב֧וֹת עַל־בָּנִ֛ים וְעַל־שִׁלֵּשִׁ֥ים וְעַל־רִבֵּעִ֖ים לְשֹׂנְאָֽי
records.gloss: Not you shall bow down to them and not you shall be made to serve them, for I, Yahweh your God, [am] a jealous God, visiting [the] iniquity of fathers on children, and on [the] third and on [the] fourth of those who hate me,
pieces: You shall neither bow to them nor serve them. For I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, am a jealous God. I bring the guilt of fathers upon their children, upon the third and the fourth generation of those who hate {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}},

L.9: You shall not bow down to them, and you shall not serve them; for I, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, [am] a jealous God, visiting [the] iniquity of fathers upon children, and upon [the] third and upon [the] fourth [generation] of those who hate {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}},

R.9: Do not bow down to them or serve them. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and I am a jealous God. I will not share your loyalty with other gods. When people hate {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, I punish their sin, even in their grandchildren and great-grandchildren.

decisions.choice: jealous: passionate, demanding sole loyalty
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 20:5: a burning claim on one who belongs to you, like a husband's claim on his wife's faithfulness, not petty envy (4:24; 6:15).

decisions.choice: visiting iniquity to the third and fourth generation of those who hate me: judgment that reaches a family that keeps hating God
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 20:5. Three or four generations could live in one household, so the sin of its head reached all who lived under it. The law did not punish children for their parents' crimes in court (24:16). Here the Hebrew adds "and" before "the third", which does not change the sense.

decisions.choice: serve them: the verb has an unusual form
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 20:5, the vowels give a form that may mean "be led into serving them". The sense is the same: Israel must not worship idols.

decisions.choice: grandchildren and great-grandchildren
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 20:5: counting the fathers as the first generation, the third and fourth are their grandchildren and great-grandchildren. Readable also adds "I will not share your loyalty" to explain "jealous".

records.source: וְעֹ֥שֶׂהחֶ֖סֶדלַֽאֲלָפִ֑יםלְאֹהֲבַ֖י וּלְשֹׁמְרֵ֥י מִצְוֺתָֽי׃ס
records.gloss: And doing covenant loyalty to thousands, to those who love me and to those who keep my commandments.
pieces: but to thousands who love {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments I show faithful love.

L.10: and doing steadfast love to thousands, to those who love {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and to those who keep {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments.

R.10: But to thousands who love {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and obey {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commands, I show faithful love.

decisions.choice: my commandments: the reading the Hebrew text marks to be read
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the Hebrew text spell "his commandments", while the scribes' note in the margin says to read "my commandments", as in Exodus 20:6. The source data follows the marked reading. "His" would refer to God in the third person in the middle of God's own speech; "my" fits the context.

decisions.choice: thousands: thousands of people, or the thousandth generation
decisions.reason: Set against "the third and the fourth" generation in verse 9, the word may mean thousands of generations, as 7:9 says ("to a thousand generations"). Either way God's love far outlasts his judgment.

decisions.choice: steadfast love: loyal love that keeps covenant
decisions.reason: Kindness that stays true to a bond and acts on it (7:9, 12; Exodus 20:6; 34:6-7). Loving God is shown by keeping what he commands (6:5-6; 11:1).

decisions.choice: steadfast love (Literal); faithful love (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 20:6. Both stress loyalty; words such as "mercy" or "kindness" leave the loyalty out.

records.source: לֹ֥א תִשָּׂ֛א אֶת־שֵֽׁם־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ לַשָּׁ֑וְא כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יְנַקֶּה֙ יְהוָ֔ה אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר־יִשָּׂ֥א אֶת־שְׁמ֖וֹ לַשָּֽׁוְא׃ס
records.gloss: Not you shall lift up [the] name of Yahweh your God to emptiness, for not will leave unpunished Yahweh [the one] who lifts up his name to emptiness.
pieces: You shall not use the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God for what is false or worthless, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will not let anyone go unpunished who uses {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name that way.

L.11: You shall not lift up the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God to emptiness, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will not leave unpunished [the one] who lifts up {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name to emptiness.

R.11: Do not use the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God in false promises or for empty purposes. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will punish anyone who treats {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name like that.

decisions.choice: lift up the name to emptiness: use God's name falsely or for nothing
decisions.reason: The same words as Exodus 20:7. To "lift up" the name is to speak it, above all in an oath (6:13; 10:20). "Emptiness" means what is false or worthless; verse 20 uses the same word of a witness. The command forbids swearing falsely by God's name and any use of it that treats it as empty.

decisions.choice: will not leave unpunished: will not acquit
decisions.reason: The verb means to declare clean or innocent. God will treat the one who misuses his name as guilty (Exodus 34:7).

decisions.choice: for what is false or worthless / in false promises or for empty purposes
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 20:7, Balanced and Readable spell out both senses of "emptiness". Literal keeps the picture.

records.source: שָׁמ֛וֹראֶת־י֥וֹםהַשַׁבָּ֖תלְקַדְּשׁ֑וֹכַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוְּךָ֖יְהוָ֥האֱלֹהֶֽיךָ
records.gloss: Keep the day of the Sabbath to make it holy, as commanded you Yahweh your God.
pieces: Keep the Sabbath day and set it apart as holy, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God commanded you.

L.12: Keep the day of the Sabbath, to make it holy, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God commanded you.

R.12: Keep the Sabbath day. Treat it as a holy day, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God commanded you.

decisions.choice: keep: in place of "remember" in Exodus 20:8
decisions.reason: Exodus 20:8 begins "Remember the day of the Sabbath". Here the verb is "keep": to guard, watch over and carry out. It is the verb of verses 1, 10 and 29 and of the Sabbath law in Exodus 31:13-16. The two verbs do not disagree: to remember the day is to keep it. "Remember" comes back in verse 15, where Israel is to remember its slavery in Egypt.

decisions.choice: as Yahweh your God commanded you: pointing back to Horeb
decisions.reason: These words are not in Exodus 20:8. Moses is retelling the ten words forty years later, and he reminds the people that the command was already given at Horeb. The same words are added to the command about parents (verse 16).

decisions.choice: make it holy: set the day apart for God
decisions.reason: The day is to be treated as different from other days, belonging to Yahweh (Exodus 16:23; 20:8; 31:14).

decisions.choice: Keep
decisions.reason: "Keep" at every level, the same word used for keeping the commandments in verses 1, 10 and 29, so the reader can see the link.

records.gloss: Six days you shall labor and you shall do all your work,
pieces: You have six days to labor and do all your work,

L.13: Six days you shall labor and do all your work,

R.13: You may work for six days and get all your jobs done.

decisions.choice: labor and do all your work: six days are given to work
decisions.reason: The same words as Exodus 20:9. The verb "labor" is the one used for serving, including Israel's hard service in Egypt, which verse 15 will recall. There is time enough in six days for all the week's work.

Do no work on it: not you, nor your son or daughter, nor your male or female servant, nor your ox or your donkey or any of your livestock, nor the foreigner living among you in your towns, so that your male and female servants may rest as you do.

L.14: but the seventh day [is] a Sabbath to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. You shall not do any work, you and your son and your daughter, and your male slave and your female slave, and your ox and your donkey and all your livestock, and your sojourner who [is] within your gates, so that your male slave and your female slave may rest like you.

R.14: But the seventh day is a Sabbath, a day of rest for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. On that day no one in your household may work: not you, not your sons or daughters, not your servants, not your ox or donkey or any of your animals, and not the foreigners who live among you in your towns. Then your servants can rest, just as you do.

decisions.choice: your ox and your donkey ... so that your servants may rest like you: additions to Exodus 20:10
decisions.reason: Exodus 20:10 says "your livestock". Here the ox and the donkey, the animals that did the heaviest work, are named first, and "all your livestock" follows. The verse also gives a purpose that Exodus does not state: the rest is so that those who serve the household may rest just as its master does. Verse 15 gives the reason.

decisions.choice: male slave, female slave: workers owned by the household
decisions.reason: The words name men and women who belonged to the household and worked for it, owned, not hired (15:12-18; Exodus 21:2-11). The command is spoken to the head of the household, who must give the day to them as to himself.

decisions.choice: your sojourner within your gates: a foreigner living in your towns
decisions.reason: A sojourner is an outsider who has settled among Israel without land or family rights (10:18-19; 24:14). "Within your gates" means inside your town.

decisions.choice: male slave, female slave (Literal); servants (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The usual rule for this word: "slave" at Literal, "servant" at Balanced and Readable, with m2 saying what their position was. In verse 15, where Israel's own slavery in Egypt is the point, every level says "slave". Exodus 20:10 has "servant" at Literal for the same words; Deuteronomy follows the style guide here, so the Literal wording of the two Decalogues differs while the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: the foreigner(s) living among you
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 20:10, Balanced and Readable say "foreigner living among you"; Literal keeps "sojourner". Readable also adds "a day of rest" to explain the word Sabbath.

records.gloss: And you shall remember that a slave you were in [the] land of Egypt, and brought you out Yahweh your God from there with a hand strong and with an arm outstretched; therefore commanded you Yahweh your God to do the day of the Sabbath.
pieces: Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God led you out from there by a strong hand and an outstretched arm. For this reason {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has commanded you to observe the Sabbath day.

L.15: And you shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God brought you out from there with a strong hand and with an outstretched arm; therefore {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God commanded you to observe the day of the Sabbath.

R.15: Remember that you were slaves in Egypt, and that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God used {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} great power to bring you out of there. That is why {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has commanded you to keep the Sabbath day.

decisions.choice: remember that you were a slave in Egypt: a different reason from Exodus 20:11
decisions.reason: In Exodus 20:11 the reason for the Sabbath is creation: God made the world in six days and rested on the seventh. Here the reason is the rescue from Egypt. A people once worked as slaves without rest, and set free by God, must give rest to those who work for them (verse 14; 15:15; 16:12; 24:18, 22). The two reasons stand side by side; neither cancels the other.

decisions.choice: a strong hand and an outstretched arm: God's power shown in the rescue
decisions.reason: The hand and the arm are pictures of strength in action. The pair describes the plagues and the crossing of the sea (4:34; 7:19; 26:8; Exodus 6:6).

decisions.choice: to do the day of the Sabbath: to observe it, to hold it as it should be held
decisions.reason: The verb is the ordinary word "do". With a festival or a holy day it means to keep or celebrate it (Exodus 31:16; Deuteronomy 16:1, 10).

decisions.choice: slave(s) at every level
decisions.reason: This is Israel's own slavery in Egypt, so "slave" stays at every level; the contrast with the servants of verse 14 is the point of the verse.

decisions.choice: used his great power
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the hand and the arm (m2).

records.gloss: Honor your father and your mother, as commanded you Yahweh your God, so that may be long your days and so that it may go well with you on the land which Yahweh your God [is] giving to you.
pieces: Honor your father and your mother, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has commanded you. Then your days will be long, and it will go well with you in the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is going to give you.

L.16: Honor your father and your mother, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God commanded you, so that your days may be long, and so that it may go well with you upon the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving to you.

R.16: Honor your father and your mother, and treat them with respect, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has commanded you. Then you will enjoy a long life, and things will go well for you in the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is about to give you.

decisions.choice: as Yahweh commanded you ... and so that it may go well with you: additions to Exodus 20:12
decisions.reason: Exodus 20:12 promises long life in the land. Here the command again points back to Horeb (as in verse 12), and a second promise is added: "that it may go well with you", a phrase Deuteronomy uses often (4:40; 6:3, 18; 22:7). Ephesians 6:2-3 quotes the command with this added promise.

decisions.choice: honor: give weight to, respect and care for
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 20:12. To honor parents is to treat them as weighty: to respect, obey and care for them all their lives (21:18-21; 27:16).

decisions.choice: the land: the ground of Canaan that God is giving
decisions.reason: The word is the one for soil and farmland. The promise is a long and good life in the land Israel is about to enter (4:40; 11:9).

records.gloss: Not you shall murder.
pieces: You shall not murder.

decisions.choice: murder: the unlawful killing of a person
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 20:13. This verb is used only of killing a human being, by intent or by careless violence (4:41-42; 19:4-6; Numbers 35:16-21), and never of killing in battle. The law itself sets the death penalty for some crimes (19:11-13), so the command forbids unlawful killing.

decisions.choice: the verse division follows the source data
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 20, the Hebrew text of the ten words carries two sets of accents, and Hebrew Bibles that follow the second set may join verses 17-20 into a single verse. The source data numbers them as four verses, so the verse numbers of this chapter are the same as in the usual numbering of translations, and no shift in numbering needs to be noted here.

records.source: וְלֹ֖אתִּנְאָֽף
records.gloss: And not you shall commit adultery.
pieces: You shall not commit adultery.

L.18: And you shall not commit adultery.

decisions.choice: and: the last commands are joined into one chain
decisions.reason: In Exodus 20:14-17 each of the last four commands stands on its own. Here each begins with "and" (verses 18-21), linking them as one series of duties toward one's neighbor.

decisions.choice: commit adultery: sexual union that breaks a marriage
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 20:14: sexual relations between a married or betrothed woman and a man who is not her husband, and both were guilty (22:22-24).

decisions.choice: no "and" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "And" at the start of verses 18-21 to show the chain (m1); in Balanced and Readable a list of commands reads more naturally without it.

records.gloss: And not you shall steal.
pieces: You shall not steal.

decisions.choice: steal: take secretly what belongs to another
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 20:15. The verb covers taking property and also taking a person to sell (24:7). The "and" is explained at verse 18.

records.gloss: And not you shall answer against your neighbor [as] a witness of emptiness.
pieces: You shall not give baseless evidence against your neighbor.

L.20: And you shall not answer against your neighbor [as] a witness of emptiness.

R.20: Do not say false or empty things about your neighbor when you are a witness.

decisions.choice: a witness of emptiness: in place of "a witness of falsehood" in Exodus 20:16
decisions.reason: Exodus 20:16 has the word for a lie. Here the word is "emptiness", the same as in verse 11 ("lift up the name to emptiness"): testimony that is groundless, worthless, false. It forbids not only an outright lie but any evidence with nothing behind it. The use of the same word links misuse of God's name and misuse of a neighbor's case.

decisions.choice: answer as a witness: testify in court
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 20:16, to "answer" is the word for giving evidence in a case. A false witness was to suffer what he meant to bring on the other (19:16-19).

decisions.choice: neighbor: a fellow member of the community
decisions.reason: The word means the person beside you: a fellow Israelite, anyone you deal with.

decisions.choice: baseless evidence / false or empty things
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the difference from Exodus 20:16 (m1): the testimony is empty, without ground. Literal keeps "a witness of emptiness".

records.gloss: And not you shall covet [the] wife of your neighbor; and not you shall desire [the] house of your neighbor, his field and his male slave and his female slave, his ox and his donkey and all that [belongs] to your neighbor.
pieces: You shall not covet your neighbor's wife. You shall not crave your neighbor's house, his field, his male or female servant, his ox or his donkey, or anything else your neighbor has.'

L.21: And you shall not covet the wife of your neighbor; and you shall not desire the house of your neighbor, his field, or his male slave, or his female slave, his ox, or his donkey, or anything that [belongs] to your neighbor.'

R.21: Do not set your heart on your neighbor's wife. Do not long to have his house, his field, his servants, his ox or donkey, or anything else that belongs to him.'

decisions.choice: the wife first, then the house and field: a different order from Exodus 20:17
decisions.reason: In Exodus 20:17 "your neighbor's house" comes first and the wife is named within the household that follows. Here the wife stands alone in the first clause, and the house begins a second list of property. The field is added, fitting a people about to receive land of their own (verse 31).

decisions.choice: covet ... desire: two verbs for wanting what is another's
decisions.reason: The first verb, as in Exodus 20:17, means to desire something in a way that leads to taking it (7:25; Joshua 7:21). The second, used here in place of Exodus's second "covet", means to long for or crave, a hunger of the appetite (Numbers 11:4). Both reach the heart, where the other wrongs begin.

decisions.choice: one command or two
decisions.reason: Because the wife and the house stand in separate clauses here, one ancient way of counting the ten words, followed in Catholic and Lutheran tradition, takes the coveting of the wife and the coveting of property as two commands, and counts verses 7-10 as one (see verse 6).

decisions.choice: the end of God's words
decisions.reason: God's words that began in verse 6 end here. Verse 22 returns to Moses' account of the events.

decisions.choice: covet ... desire (Literal); covet ... crave (Balanced); set your heart on ... long to have (Readable)
decisions.reason: Each level uses two different words, since the Hebrew does. As in verse 14, the servants are "slave" at Literal and "servant" at Balanced and Readable. Exodus 20:17 has "servant" at Literal; the difference is one of wording only (see verse 14).

records.gloss: These words spoke Yahweh to all your assembly on the mountain from [the] midst of the fire, the cloud and the thick darkness, [with] a voice great, and not he added; and he wrote them on two tablets of stones and gave them to me.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke these words to your whole assembly at the mountain, in a great voice out of the fire, the cloud and the thick darkness, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said no more. He wrote them on two tablets of stone and gave them to me.

L.22: These words {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to all your assembly on the mountain from the midst of the fire, the cloud, and the thick darkness, [with] a great voice, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} added no more; and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wrote them on two tablets of stone and gave them to me.

R.22: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke these words in a loud voice to all of you gathered at the mountain. He spoke from the fire, the cloud and the thick darkness, and then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said nothing more. He wrote the words on two tablets made of stone and gave them to me.

decisions.choice: and he added no more: these words and nothing else
alternatives: and he did not stop speaking
decisions.reason: God spoke the ten words to the whole people and then spoke no further words to them directly. The rest of the law came through Moses (verses 27-31). The ten words therefore stand apart from all the other laws. An old Aramaic rendering took the phrase as "and he did not stop", that is, God's voice never ceased; the plain sense of the Hebrew here is "he added no more".

decisions.choice: two tablets of stone: the covenant written by God
decisions.reason: God wrote the ten words on two stone tablets and gave them to Moses (4:13; 9:10; Exodus 24:12; 31:18). Chapters 9-10 tell how the tablets were broken and written again (10:1-5).

decisions.choice: thick darkness: a dense, dark cloud
decisions.reason: The word names the deep, dark cloud in which God was hidden on the mountain (4:11; Exodus 20:21).

decisions.choice: assembly: the people gathered as one body
decisions.reason: The word names Israel gathered before God. Deuteronomy calls this "the day of the assembly" (9:10; 10:4; 18:16).

decisions.choice: split into sentences
decisions.reason: Readable splits the long verse into short sentences and repeats "He spoke"; it says "all of you gathered" for "your assembly".

records.heading: Out of the fire

records.source: וַיְהִ֗י כְּשָׁמְעֲכֶ֤ם אֶת־הַקּוֹל֙ מִתּ֣וֹךְ הַחֹ֔שֶׁךְ וְהָהָ֖ר בֹּעֵ֣ר בָּאֵ֑שׁ וַתִּקְרְב֣וּן אֵלַ֔י כָּל־רָאשֵׁ֥י שִׁבְטֵיכֶ֖ם וְזִקְנֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And it was, when you heard the voice from [the] midst of the darkness, and the mountain [was] burning with fire, and you drew near to me, all [the] heads of your tribes and your elders,
pieces: When you heard the voice coming out of the darkness and the mountain was burning with fire, all your tribal heads and your elders came near to me,

L.23: And it happened, when you heard the voice from the midst of the darkness, and the mountain [was] burning with fire, that you came near to me, all the heads of your tribes and your elders,

R.23: You heard the voice from the darkness, and you saw the mountain burning with fire. Then all the leaders of your tribes and your elders came to me.

decisions.choice: the voice: God's voice speaking the ten words
decisions.reason: The voice is the one that spoke from the fire (verses 22, 24). The people's response follows in verses 24-27.

decisions.choice: the heads of your tribes and your elders: the people's leaders, speaking for all
decisions.reason: The leaders of the tribes and the elders acted for the whole people (1:13-15; 29:9; Exodus 19:7). Moses still says "you": what they said, the people said.

decisions.choice: you saw
decisions.reason: Readable makes two sentences and supplies "you saw" for the burning mountain; it says "leaders" for "heads". Balanced says "tribal heads".

records.source: וַתֹּאמְר֗וּ הֵ֣ן הֶרְאָ֜נוּ יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֵ֨ינוּ֙ אֶת־כְּבֹד֣וֹ וְאֶת־גָּדְל֔וֹ וְאֶת־קֹל֥וֹ שָׁמַ֖עְנוּ מִתּ֣וֹךְ הָאֵ֑שׁ הַיּ֤וֹם הַזֶּה֙ רָאִ֔ינוּ כִּֽי־יְדַבֵּ֧ר אֱלֹהִ֛ים אֶת־הָֽאָדָ֖ם וָחָֽי׃
records.gloss: And you said, look, has shown us Yahweh our God his glory and his greatness, and his voice we have heard from [the] midst of the fire; the day the this we have seen that speaks God with the man and he lives.
pieces: and you said, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} our God has shown us {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} greatness, and we have heard {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice out of the fire. Today we have seen that God may speak with {{gender:a person|a man}}, and {{gender:that person|he}} may still live.

L.24: and you said, 'Look, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God has shown us {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} greatness, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice we have heard from the midst of the fire. This day we have seen that God speaks with {{gender:humankind|man}}, and {{gender:they live|he lives}}.

R.24: You said, 'Look! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} our God has shown us {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} great power. We have heard {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice from the fire. Today we have seen that God can speak to people and they can still live.

decisions.choice: glory and greatness: the splendor and power of God's presence
decisions.reason: "Glory" comes from a root meaning heavy: the weight and splendor of God made visible, here in the fire on the mountain (Exodus 24:16-17). "Greatness" is his might (3:24; 11:2).

decisions.choice: God speaks with a human and that one lives: a wonder, not the expected outcome
decisions.reason: Scripture often says that no one can see God and live (Exodus 33:20; Judges 13:22). The people are amazed to have heard him and survived (4:33). The next verse draws the opposite fear: it may not happen twice.

decisions.choice: the man: a human being, anyone
decisions.reason: With the article, the word here means humankind or any human being, man or woman, set against God.

decisions.choice: gender span for the human being
decisions.reason: The word means a human being of either sex (m3), so Literal and Balanced use the inclusive form by default, with "man ... he" as the setting; Readable's "people" needs no span.

decisions.choice: no "Look" (Balanced)
decisions.reason: Balanced leaves the opening "look" unsaid; its force is carried by the plain statement. Literal and Readable keep it.

records.gloss: And now, why should we die? For will consume us the fire the great the this; if [are] continuing we to hear the voice of Yahweh our God again, and we will die.
pieces: So why should we die now? This great fire will devour us. If we go on hearing the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, we will die.

L.25: And now, why should we die? For this great fire will consume us. If we continue to hear the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God any longer, then we will die.

R.25: Why should we die? This huge fire will burn us up. If we hear the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God again, we will die.

decisions.choice: and now, why should we die: a conclusion drawn from verse 24
decisions.reason: "And now" turns from what has happened to what should be done. They have lived once; they ask why they should risk death again.

decisions.choice: the fire will consume us: fear before God's holiness
decisions.reason: The people are not rejecting God's word but fear the holiness of his presence, which they cannot bear (Exodus 20:18-19). God approves of their fear in verses 28-29.

records.source: כִּ֣י מִ֣י כָל־בָּשָׂ֡ר אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁמַ֣ע קוֹל֩ אֱלֹהִ֨ים חַיִּ֜ים מְדַבֵּ֧ר מִתּוֹךְ־הָאֵ֛שׁ כָּמֹ֖נוּ וַיֶּֽחִי׃
records.gloss: For who [is] all flesh who has heard [the] voice of God living speaking from [the] midst of the fire like us and lived?
pieces: Of all mortals, who has heard the voice of the living God speak from the fire as we have, and stayed alive?

L.26: For who [is there] of all flesh who has heard the voice of [the] living God speaking from the midst of the fire, as we [have], and lived?

R.26: Has any human being ever heard the living God speak from the middle of a fire, as we have, and stayed alive?

decisions.choice: all flesh: every human being, frail and mortal
decisions.reason: "Flesh" stands for human beings in their weakness and mortality, set against the living God (Genesis 6:12; Isaiah 40:6).

decisions.choice: the living God: God who is alive and acts
decisions.reason: Unlike idols, which cannot speak or hear (4:28), this God speaks. In Hebrew both the word for God and "living" are plural in form, as usual with this title.

decisions.choice: who: a question that expects the answer "no one"
decisions.reason: The question is a way of saying that this has never happened to anyone else (4:32-33).

records.source: קְרַ֤ב אַתָּה֙ וּֽשֲׁמָ֔ע אֵ֛ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֹאמַ֖ר יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ וְאַ֣תְּ׀תְּדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלֵ֗ינוּ אֵת֩ כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֨ר יְדַבֵּ֜ר יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֵ֛ינוּ אֵלֶ֖יךָ וְשָׁמַ֥עְנוּ וְעָשִֽׂינוּ׃
records.gloss: Draw near you and hear all that will say Yahweh our God, and you, you shall speak to us all that will speak Yahweh our God to you, and we will hear and we will do.
pieces: You go near and hear all that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God says, and then you tell us all that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God tells you; we will listen and do it.'

L.27: You draw near and hear all that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God says, and you, you shall speak to us all that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God speaks to you, and we will hear and do [it].'

R.27: You go close and hear everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God says. Then pass on to us all that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God tells you. We will listen and do it.'

decisions.choice: you ... you: Moses and not the people
decisions.reason: The Hebrew adds the pronoun "you" twice for emphasis: Moses, not they, is to go near and to pass on God's words.

decisions.choice: you: written in an unusual form
decisions.reason: The second "you" is spelled with the form that usually addresses a woman. It refers to Moses; the same spelling is found where Moses speaks to God (Numbers 11:15). It does not change the sense.

decisions.choice: hear and do: listen and obey
decisions.reason: The verb "hear" also means to heed. With "do" it is a promise of obedience, as at Horeb (Exodus 19:8; 24:3, 7).

decisions.choice: the end of the people's words
decisions.reason: The words of the people that began in verse 24 end here.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע יְהוָה֙ אֶת־ק֣וֹל דִּבְרֵיכֶ֔ם בְּדַבֶּרְכֶ֖ם אֵלָ֑י וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י שָׁ֠מַעְתִּי אֶת־ק֨וֹל דִּבְרֵ֜י הָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבְּר֣וּ אֵלֶ֔יךָ הֵיטִ֖יבוּ כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֵּֽרוּ׃
records.gloss: And heard Yahweh [the] sound of your words when you spoke to me, and said Yahweh to me, I have heard [the] sound of [the] words of the people the this which they spoke to you; they have done well [in] all that they spoke.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} heard what you said when you spoke to me, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, 'I have heard what this people said to you. They have spoken well in everything they said.

L.28: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} heard the sound of your words when you spoke to me, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, 'I have heard the sound of the words of this people, which they have spoken to you. They have done well [in] all that they have spoken.

R.28: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} heard what you said to me. He said to me, 'I have heard what these people said to you. They were right to say all this.

decisions.choice: the sound of your words: what you said
decisions.reason: "The sound of the words" simply means the words spoken. God heard the people's request as they made it to Moses.

decisions.choice: they have done well: God approves their request
decisions.reason: God agrees that Moses should stand between him and the people. 18:16-18 looks back to this moment when it promises a prophet like Moses.

decisions.choice: God's words, from here to the end of verse 31
decisions.reason: God's reply to Moses runs from this verse to verse 31. Moses quotes it within his own speech.

records.source: מִֽי־יִתֵּ֡ן וְהָיָה֩ לְבָבָ֨ם זֶ֜ה לָהֶ֗ם לְיִרְאָ֥ה אֹתִ֛י וְלִשְׁמֹ֥ר אֶת־כָּל־מִצְוֺתַ֖י כָּל־הַיָּמִ֑ים לְמַ֨עַן יִיטַ֥ב לָהֶ֛ם וְלִבְנֵיהֶ֖ם לְעֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: Who will give, and would be this heart of theirs to them, to fear me and to keep all my commandments all the days, so that it may go well with them and with their children forever!
pieces: If only their hearts would stay like this, so that they would fear {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and keep all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments always, and it would go well with them and with their children forever!

L.29: Who will grant that this heart of theirs would be theirs, to fear {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and to keep all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments all the days, so that it may go well with them and with their children forever!

R.29: I wish they would always have hearts like this, so that they would fear {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and obey all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commands. Then things would go well for them and their children forever!

decisions.choice: who will give: if only, a wish
decisions.reason: "Who will give" is a common Hebrew way of expressing a strong wish (28:67; Exodus 16:3; Numbers 11:29). Here it is God who longs for his people's faithfulness.

decisions.choice: heart: the mind and will
decisions.reason: The heart is the place of thought, will and choice, not only of feeling. God wishes that their present attitude would last (6:5-6; 10:16).

decisions.choice: fear me: reverent awe that leads to obedience
decisions.reason: To fear God is to take him with full seriousness and so to obey him, as the next words say (4:10; 6:2, 24; 10:12).

decisions.choice: this heart of theirs would be theirs
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew's double "theirs" ("their heart ... to them"); Balanced and Readable say it once.

records.source: לֵ֖ךְ אֱמֹ֣ר לָהֶ֑ם שׁ֥וּבוּ לָכֶ֖ם לְאָהֳלֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Go, say to them, return for yourselves to your tents.
pieces: Go and tell them, "Go back to your tents."

L.30: Go, say to them, "Return to your tents."

R.30: Go and tell them to go back home to their tents.

decisions.choice: return to your tents: the gathering at the mountain is over
decisions.reason: The people had been called to stand at the foot of the mountain (Exodus 19:10-17). Now they are sent back to their camp, while Moses stays (verse 31).

decisions.choice: for yourselves: a word that marks the action as their own
decisions.reason: The Hebrew adds "for yourselves" after "return", as it often does with verbs of going; it adds no further meaning.

decisions.choice: reported speech
decisions.reason: Readable gives God's message as reported speech, to avoid a quotation within a quotation within Moses' speech.

records.source: וְאַתָּ֗ה פֹּה֮ עֲמֹ֣ד עִמָּדִי֒ וַאֲדַבְּרָ֣ה אֵלֶ֗יךָ אֵ֧ת כָּל־הַמִּצְוָ֛ה וְהַחֻקִּ֥ים וְהַמִּשְׁפָּטִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר תְּלַמְּדֵ֑ם וְעָשׂ֣וּ בָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֧ר אָנֹכִ֛י נֹתֵ֥ן לָהֶ֖ם לְרִשְׁתָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And you, here stand with me, and I will speak to you all the commandment and the statutes and the judgments which you shall teach them, and they shall do [them] in the land which I [am] giving to them to possess it.
pieces: But you, stay here with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I will tell you the whole commandment, the statutes and the rulings that you are to teach them, so that they may do them in the land I am giving them to take possession of.'

L.31: But you, stand here with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I will speak to you all the commandment and the statutes and the judgments that you shall teach them, and they shall do [them] in the land that I [am] giving to them to take possession of it.'

R.31: But you stay here with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I will tell you all the commands, laws and rules. Teach them to the people so that they will obey them in the land I am giving them to take as their own.'

decisions.choice: the commandment: the whole of what God commands
decisions.reason: The word is singular: the commandment as one whole, which the statutes and judgments then spell out (6:1; 7:11).

decisions.choice: which you shall teach them: what Moses is now doing
decisions.reason: Moses says that the laws he is about to teach in Moab (verse 1; 6:1; 12:1) are the ones God gave him at Horeb, when the people went back to their tents.

decisions.choice: to possess it: to take the land and hold it as their own
decisions.reason: The verb means to take possession, to inherit, often by driving out those who held it before (1:8; 4:1).

decisions.choice: the end of God's words
decisions.reason: God's reply that began in verse 28 ends here; in verse 32 Moses speaks to the people again.

decisions.choice: all the commands
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plural, which a new reader understands as "all that God commands"; Literal and Balanced keep the singular "commandment" (m1).

records.source: וּשְׁמַרְתֶּ֣ם לַעֲשׂ֔וֹת כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוָּ֛ה יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֖ם אֶתְכֶ֑ם לֹ֥א תָסֻ֖רוּ יָמִ֥ין וּשְׂמֹֽאל׃
records.gloss: And you shall take care to do as commanded Yahweh your God you; not you shall turn aside right or left.
pieces: Take care, then, to do just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has commanded you, turning neither to the right nor to the left.

L.32: And you shall take care to do as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has commanded you; you shall not turn aside [to the] right or [to the] left.

R.32: Make sure you obey all that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has commanded you. Do not wander off the path, either to the right or to the left.

decisions.choice: you shall take care: Moses draws the conclusion
decisions.reason: Moses now speaks to the people again, in the plural: because God gave these laws at Horeb, they must be careful to do them (verse 1).

decisions.choice: turn aside to the right or left: leave the path
decisions.reason: God's commands are pictured as a road. To turn aside either way is to leave it at all (17:11, 20; 28:14; Joshua 1:7). Verse 33 continues the picture.

decisions.choice: the path
decisions.reason: Readable supplies "path" to show that the picture is of a road, which verse 33 names.

records.source: בְּכָל־הַדֶּ֗רֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֜ה יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֛ם אֶתְכֶ֖ם תֵּלֵ֑כוּ לְמַ֤עַן תִּֽחְיוּן֙ וְט֣וֹב לָכֶ֔ם וְהַאֲרַכְתֶּ֣ם יָמִ֔ים בָּאָ֖רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר תִּֽירָשֽׁוּן׃
records.gloss: In all the way which commanded Yahweh your God you, you shall walk, so that you may live and [it] be well with you and you prolong days in the land which you will possess.
pieces: Walk in every part of the way that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has commanded you. Then you will live, it will be well with you, and your days will be long in the land you are going to take possession of.

L.33: In all the way that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has commanded you, you shall walk, so that you may live, and [it may be] well with you, and you may prolong [your] days in the land that you will take possession of.

R.33: Follow the whole way that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has commanded you. Then you will live, things will go well for you, and you will have a long life in the land you will take as your own.

decisions.choice: walk in the way: live by what God commands
decisions.reason: To walk is to live and act; "the way" is the path God has set out (8:6; 10:12; 11:22).

decisions.choice: so that you may live: life and good in the land as the fruit of obedience
decisions.reason: Moses ties obedience to life, good and long years in the land (4:1, 40; 6:24; 30:15-20). The speech goes on into chapter 6.

decisions.choice: possess: take the land as your own
decisions.reason: As in verse 31.

decisions.choice: Follow the whole way
decisions.reason: Readable says "follow" for "walk in", so that "you will live" is not said twice in one sentence.
